fullData.title: The Angry Storm at Blue Heron Lake
fullData.passage: The afternoon air grew heavy as the dark clouds marched aggressively across the sky. The wind howled a terrifying song through the pine trees, waking up the sleepy lake. Suddenly, million-pound raindrops crashed down onto the wooden dock with a deafening roar. The water shivered under the attack of the fierce storm.

instances.text: the dark clouds marched aggressively across the sky
instances.literalMeaning: The dark clouds moved quickly and menacingly across the sky.
instances.explanation: Clouds cannot actually march like soldiers, so this gives a human action to non-human things.

instances.text: The wind howled a terrifying song
instances.literalMeaning: The wind made a loud, scary noise as it blew.
instances.explanation: Wind cannot howl or sing songs like a person or animal.

instances.literalMeaning: Very heavy and large raindrops fell down hard.
instances.explanation: Raindrops do not actually weigh a million pounds; this is an extreme exaggeration to show how heavy the rain was.

instances.literalMeaning: The surface of the lake rippled from the wind and rain.
instances.explanation: Water does not have feelings and cannot shiver from cold or fear like a human.
